name: Gum massage (Stillman technique)
lead: The Stillman technique is a toothbrushing method named for a dental researcher, associated with gentle gum stimulation or massage alongside cleaning at the gumline. Gum massage is discussed in online circles as a way to improve gum health.

The pages consulted for this article do not describe the Stillman method or gum massage, so evidence is limited here. Wikipedia notes that technique advice from dental associations, companies and textbooks has been inconsistent, and that lay people clean at most about 40% of tooth margins at the gumline.[1]

paras: General guidance reported includes avoiding hard pressure and horizontal scrubbing at the necks of teeth.[1] Harder brushes remove plaque more efficiently but stress teeth and gums more; a 2011 study rated a medium-to-soft brush used longer as the best compromise.[1]
No studies found. The sources consulted do not summarise trials of the Stillman technique or gum massage.

card.summary: A gumline brushing/gum-massage method; little evidence was found in the sources reviewed.
card.note: Hard pressure on gums is cautioned against in general guidance.

quick.overview:
The Stillman technique is a brushing method involving gentle gumline action, sometimes described as gum massage.

No trial evidence was found in the sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say stimulating the gums improves circulation and plaque removal at the gumline.
quick.risks: General guidance cautions against pressing hard on teeth and gums.
